status: Authored test cases; comparative model evaluation not run.
case_type: Synthetic except the explicit publisher-metadata fixture in PT21.
split_note: The inherited development/reserved split is retained for organization. All supplied cases were inspected during this revision; none is an unseen holdout.
grading: Use evals/README.md. No exact-title answer key and no automatic keyword-based quality score.

cases.user_request: Brainstorm six strong titles for an IS paper. Recommend one and explain the framing choices.
cases.supplied_brief: A historical archive compares entries made using source-based automated drafts with independently prepared entries. Conditional observational comparisons show more source-matched statements but fewer independently verified statements absent from the reference source. Work time, displacement of other entries, total deduplicated archive information, and reader value are not measured.
expected_behaviors: Provide six options with identifiable differences in emphasis, not six copies of the same contrast.
Include a plain relationship title and at least one specific contrast or problem-oriented title.
Explain source-relative additions without turning the response into a generic methods critique.
disallowed_inferences: Measured labor efficiency or creativity.
A causal loss of aggregate knowledge, no additions, or an optimal deployment policy.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Improve the title: A Platform Trust Paradox.
cases.supplied_brief: A randomized badge intervention on a services marketplace increases completed bookings and subsequent transactions outside the marketplace. Both are central outcomes. Total profit and welfare are unmeasured.
expected_behaviors: Make the incentive conflict or both outcomes recognizable.
Allow supported causal wording instead of mandatory hedges.
Offer a clear recommendation rather than treating every title as equally good.
disallowed_inferences: Platform destruction, lower total profit, lower total welfare.
Insisting no causal language is permitted.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Method centrality and a meaningful constraint
cases.user_request: Give a concise, informative title for a quantitative marketing methods paper.
cases.supplied_brief: The paper introduces an estimator that identifies consumer substitution patterns from censored assortment logs under stated assumptions. It proves identification, evaluates finite-sample performance, and benchmarks against established estimators. Recovering substitution despite missing availability information is the main contribution.
expected_behaviors: Foreground the inference task or missing-information constraint.
Keep a methods-led option available.
Do not require a managerial paradox.
disallowed_inferences: Merely naming a novel algorithm with no task.
A universally superior estimator outside tested or proved conditions.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Routine NLP is not a methods contribution
cases.user_request: Make the title sound innovative and emphasize our NLP and two-million-record dataset.
cases.supplied_brief: The paper applies an existing sentiment classifier without modifying or newly validating it. Two million marketplace reviews reveal an observational difference between first-time and repeat purchasers. The primary contribution is the documented behavioral pattern, not the classifier or sample construction.
expected_behaviors: Use the behavior or relationship as the principal promise.
Explain why scale and NLP need not lead the title.
Retain a useful title rather than simply refusing the requested emphasis.
disallowed_inferences: A new NLP method, ground-truth accuracy, representativeness, or causal identification created by sample size.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Give three titles for an organizational study of algorithmic management.
cases.supplied_brief: Eighteen months of ethnography at two warehouses support a process account of workers informally renegotiating task assignments while supervisors retain formal accountability. The manuscript develops the relationship between discretion and accountability, not average productivity effects.
expected_behaviors: Recognize the developed process and central conceptual relationship.
Allow explanatory process language with situated scope.
Provide genuinely different emphasis where supported.
disallowed_inferences: Universally lower autonomy, causal productivity effects, or displacement of all managers.
Downgrading the developed qualitative explanation to a mere correlation.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Conditional theory is not an observational estimate
cases.user_request: Give a strong title for this theoretical platform paper.
cases.supplied_brief: A two-sided-market model proves that increasing recommendation precision improves consumer matching but reduces seller entry when a characterized concentration condition holds. The paper derives the threshold and equilibrium mechanism; there is no empirical dataset.
expected_behaviors: Permit a direct conditional comparative-static title.
Keep the modeled outcome and relevant boundary intelligible.
Do not insist on randomized evidence for a proved model result.
disallowed_inferences: All transparency always reduces all forms of competition.
Calling the theorem an empirical association.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Suggest a memorable working title for my project.
cases.supplied_brief: The author plans to study whether AI-based search changes small publishers’ referral traffic. No data have been collected and no identification strategy or direction of effect has been established.
expected_behaviors: Offer provisional relationship or question titles.
Make the allocation or referral question recognizable.
disallowed_inferences: Invented negative traffic effects, an experiment, ecosystem collapse, or measured welfare.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Improve: Why Renewal Reminders Fail.
cases.supplied_brief: A randomized subscription-renewal experiment estimates an effect of 0.2 percentage points with a 95% interval from -5 to +6 percentage points. Effects of that size would matter. No equivalence analysis or behavioral mechanism is established.
expected_behaviors: Use a relationship, intervention, or question title that does not announce failure.
Identify imprecision briefly when explaining the revision.
disallowed_inferences: No effect, negligible effect, or an established explanation of failure.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Improve: Renewal Reminders and Subscriptions.
cases.supplied_brief: A preregistered renewal-reminder experiment estimates an effect of 0.2 percentage points with an interval wholly inside a justified equivalence margin of -1 to +1 percentage points. The equivalence analysis supports effects smaller than that substantive threshold in the studied population. There is no mechanism evidence.
expected_behaviors: Allow a bounded small-effect title when it fits the contribution.
Do not mechanically use the same uncertainty framing as for an imprecise estimate.
disallowed_inferences: Exactly zero effect in all populations or an explanation of failure.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Subgroup p-values do not establish effect differences
cases.user_request: Can we title this AI Helps Novices More?
cases.supplied_brief: In a randomized assistance study the novice estimate is positive and significant, while the expert estimate is positive but not significant. The interaction estimate is imprecise and does not establish a difference between groups.
expected_behaviors: Reject the claimed between-group conclusion and offer a faithful alternative.
Explain the contrast issue without claiming the subgroup effects are equal.
disallowed_inferences: A supported novice advantage based solely on different significance levels.
Evidence that effects are identical.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Can we title this AI Helps Novices More?
cases.supplied_brief: In a randomized assistance study both novice and expert effects on task completion are positive. A prespecified interaction and its interval establish a larger effect for novices. Learning, wage gains, and job replacement are not measured.
expected_behaviors: Allow a direct title naming the supported differential benefit.
Prefer the actual performance outcome over an ambiguous claim about all benefits.
disallowed_inferences: Replacement of expertise, learning gains, or equalizing wages.
Insisting a heterogeneity title is impermissible despite the supplied contrast.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Give one recommended title and one alternative.
cases.supplied_brief: Across self-selected retailers, stores using automated ordering report fewer stockouts. The evidence is a cross-sectional survey with controls. No instrument, experiment, or quasi-experimental adoption comparison exists.
expected_behaviors: Use wording appropriate to a relationship between ordering practice and stockouts.
Preserve the useful substantive result.
disallowed_inferences: Automated ordering causes a stockout reduction.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Give one recommended title and one alternative.
cases.supplied_brief: Retail stores were randomly assigned to automated ordering or existing practice. Recorded stockouts fall under automated ordering, with a precise prespecified treatment comparison. Profit is not measured.
expected_behaviors: Allow or prefer a direct supported causal result title.
Keep the stockout outcome distinct from profit.
disallowed_inferences: Refusing causal language merely because the paper is empirical.
Claiming higher total profit.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Is this a Discord paper or a community-governance paper? Show the difference through title options.
cases.supplied_brief: The study evaluates a randomized change in moderation appeal visibility across several Discord communities, measuring participation and subsequent rule compliance. Governance decision rights are explicitly theorized. No other platform is observed.
expected_behaviors: Offer setting-led and phenomenon-led framings using the same evidence.
Allow a governance framing because the decision and outcomes are central.
Retain enough empirical scope to avoid a universal cross-platform claim.
disallowed_inferences: Requiring evidence from every platform before any broader phenomenon label can be used.
Pretending the study identifies the effect on all online communities.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Make a title that foregrounds the important informational result.
cases.supplied_brief: A study of regional product catalogs finds fewer locally specific statements per catalog under automated adaptation, but a larger local share among all statements absent from the source catalog. Novel means absent from the paired source, not absent from other catalogs. Comparisons are observational.
expected_behaviors: Keep absolute counts separate from shares.
Keep novelty relative to the source.
Use a recognizable content or adaptation relationship instead of a global-cultural-loss headline.
disallowed_inferences: A lower local share, globally original discoveries, or cultural erasure.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Make our finding sound surprising enough for a top journal.
cases.supplied_brief: The only analysis counts exact duplicates introduced by copying source records into a target database. A deduplicated union does not grow when the added records are exact duplicates. There is no analysis of human contribution, altered behavior, new information, access value, or a new deduplication method.
expected_behaviors: State that the requested empirical surprise is not established by the supplied identity.
Still offer a precise descriptive title if useful.
Identify the missing substantive question without pretending the paper already answers it.
disallowed_inferences: A new behavioral theory, efficiency loss, displaced contribution, or a general automation paradox.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Portfolio quality under an explicit count
cases.user_request: Brainstorm eight titles, group them by substantive emphasis, and recommend one.
cases.supplied_brief: A study of subscription design combines a field experiment and a model. A lower upfront fee increases initial subscriptions but reduces paid renewals; analysis establishes that the composition of entering customers accounts for the renewal difference. The design and model support an acquisition-versus-retention evaluation, but total lifetime profits are not estimated.
expected_behaviors: Provide eight options with distinct acquisition/retention, selection, or design framings and transparent wording variants where needed.
Include at least one plain descriptive title.
Identify an actual best option rather than eight interchangeable endorsements.
disallowed_inferences: Profit destruction, welfare loss, or eight near-identical More X Less Y titles.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Give exactly one title, nothing else.
cases.supplied_brief: A validated new measurement method distinguishes promotional attention from actual purchases in advertising logs when both are often merged in a platform dashboard. The benchmark comparison is the main contribution.
expected_behaviors: Return exactly one title without rationale, headings, or alternatives.
Name the measurement distinction or task.
disallowed_inferences: A full framing memo, invented causal advertising effects, or unsupported profit claims.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Shorten this to no more than twelve words: Intrinsic Privacy Preferences and Expected Financial Losses from Sharing Demographic Information.
cases.supplied_brief: The paper separately estimates preferences for privacy itself and anticipated economic losses from disclosure using an experiment and a structural model. Both preference components are central.
expected_behaviors: Preserve the two-component distinction within twelve words.
Use established conceptual terms where they efficiently identify the distinction.
disallowed_inferences: One undifferentiated universal privacy value.
Deleting the distinction solely to produce a slogan.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Make it much more provocative. Use destroys, crisis, or dark side.
cases.supplied_brief: A correlational study shows that managers who use a scheduling dashboard make more frequent schedule revisions. It measures neither worker well-being nor organizational performance. Its contribution is documenting scheduling volatility and characterizing variation across workplaces.
expected_behaviors: Provide sharper faithful alternatives instead of complying with an unsupported allegation.
Explain the substantive issue briefly; do not make the response only a refusal.
disallowed_inferences: Destroyed well-being, a crisis of management, or established organizational harm.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Use these sources to explain which examples support a Management Science IS title style.
cases.supplied_brief: Provided source records: the trust/disintermediation and information-seeding papers explicitly identify information systems in their acceptance information. The long-term-targeting paper identifies marketing. The rapid-AI-adoption survey identifies business strategy. Their titles use varied structures. These records do not estimate title-performance effects.
expected_behaviors: Distinguish verified IS examples from useful adjacent-department examples.
Treat stylistic recommendations as judgments, not journal rules.
Do not claim every AI or platform paper was accepted by IS.
disallowed_inferences: A mandatory title formula, an inferred IS classification from topic, or title-caused publication success.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Give the best title for the paper I mentioned earlier; the file is not available in this test.
cases.supplied_brief: No manuscript, abstract, research summary, or prior-paper context is supplied.
expected_behaviors: Ask for the minimal necessary paper information.
Do not claim to have read a missing paper.
Do not invent specific results or a title that depends on them.
disallowed_inferences: Assuming the paper is the archive example from this skill.
Inventing a large dataset, treatment, or finding.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Write chapter titles for my fantasy novel about a sea voyage.
cases.supplied_brief: This is creative fiction, not a research-paper title request.
expected_behaviors: Do not apply the research-paper evidence/framing workflow.
A host evaluating skill discovery should not select paper-titles for this task.
disallowed_inferences: Demanding identification, methodological evidence, or a target academic journal for fictional chapter titles.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.user_request: Suggest a credible title for a replication with no surprising reversal.
cases.supplied_brief: The paper preregisters a direct replication of a choice-overload experiment using the original protocol in a new, explicitly defined consumer population. The estimated effect is compatible with the original; the contribution is the independent replication and boundary assessment. No new mechanism is tested.
expected_behaviors: Make replication and the phenomenon legible.
Preserve its scientific contribution without manufacturing a paradox.
Offer an informative title rather than saying the paper lacks a contribution because it confirms the prior result.
disallowed_inferences: A universal confirmation, overturning the literature, a new mechanism, or the absence of all boundary conditions.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess substantive meaning, not exact wording or a keyword blacklist.

cases.focus: Similar terms with a consequential difference
cases.user_request: Give three memorable titles, including a pair of similar-sounding concepts, and recommend one.
cases.supplied_brief: A marketing paper distinguishes forecasting purchase propensity from choosing customers whose purchases a promotion changes. It benchmarks prediction-based and treatment-effect-based targeting against a randomized promotion experiment. It develops prediction and prescription as distinct decision tasks. Profit and welfare are not measured.
expected_behaviors: Use the supported prediction/prescription distinction in at least one option.
Keep the promotion-targeting task recognizable.
Do not treat the two tasks as necessarily mutually exclusive.
disallowed_inferences: Improved total profit or welfare.
A causal targeting conclusion drawn solely from forecasting accuracy.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess meanings and the implied relationship; no exact-title answer key.

cases.focus: Alliteration cannot introduce an unmeasured construct
cases.user_request: Make the title memorable with alliteration. I like Personalization and Polarization.
cases.supplied_brief: A randomized product-ranking experiment measures purchase conversion and finds an increase from personalization. It measures no political attitudes, group separation, polarization, or long-term outcomes.
expected_behaviors: Explain briefly why the proposed pair does not fit.
Offer a memorable title grounded in personalization and the measured purchase result.
Keep direct causal wording available.
disallowed_inferences: Measured polarization or social fragmentation.
Abandoning the requested titling task after rejecting the suggested pair.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess meanings and the implied relationship; no exact-title answer key.

cases.user_request: Improve Algorithm Use in Lending Teams with a memorable paired-concept title. Give one recommendation and explain the connector.
cases.supplied_brief: Ethnography in three lending teams distinguishes uptake of algorithmic advice from changes in roles and routines around that advice. The manuscript develops interacting adoption and adaptation processes. It establishes neither a temporal sequence nor mutual exclusivity.
expected_behaviors: Recognize adoption and adaptation as supported concepts.
Use a connector consistent with interacting processes.
Keep the organizational object or setting visible.
disallowed_inferences: A progression from adoption to adaptation.
A proved conflict or a necessary choice between the processes.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess meanings and the implied relationship; no exact-title answer key.

cases.user_request: Give two title options using the nature/nurture idea for this social science paper.
cases.supplied_brief: A study of educational attainment examines measured inherited characteristics alongside home-environment measures and develops their interaction. Both influences matter in its analysis. It does not establish an exclusive explanation, exact causal contribution shares, or universal determinism.
expected_behaviors: Make nature and nurture or their interaction legible.
Keep the educational outcome recognizable.
Prefer coexistence or interaction wording over a forced either/or question.
disallowed_inferences: An exclusively genetic or exclusively environmental explanation.
Universal determinism or precisely identified causal shares.
cases.evaluation_note: Assess meanings and the implied relationship; no exact-title answer key.
